title: Hello World and basic arithmetic
description:
Write a script that prints "Hello World!", then the result of each of these arithmetic operations, one per line, in order: `2 + 3`, `3 - 1`, `2 * 3`, `3 + 2`, `3 - 2`, `3 * 2`, `3 / 2`, `3 ** 2`, `3 % 2`, `3 // 2`.

This is Day 1's real content: unlike every other day, the source repository has no numbered exercise list for Day 1 - just a single walkthrough script (01_Day_Introduction/helloworld.py). This exercise reproduces that script.
hints: Each line is its own print() call: one for the greeting text, then one per arithmetic expression, in the exact order listed above.

/ always gives a float result (even 3 / 2 -> 1.5), while // (floor division) and % (modulus/remainder) both give whole-number results for these inputs - that's why the last two lines are 1 and 1, not decimals.
expected_behavior: Prints the greeting, then the ten arithmetic results, each on its own line.
solution:
print("Hello World!")

print(2 + 3)
print(3 - 1)
print(2 * 3)
print(3 + 2)
print(3 - 2)
print(3 * 2)
print(3 / 2)
print(3 ** 2)
print(3 % 2)
print(3 // 2)
explanation: Each operator does exactly what its symbol suggests, applied to two small integers - the only one that might surprise is /, which always produces a float in Python 3 even when the division is exact in a different sense than // is.
